title: Matter — Properties and Changes
description: Explore physical and chemical properties of matter and how matter changes.

lessons.title: Properties of Matter
lessons.content: Matter has physical properties (observable without changing the substance) and chemical properties (how it reacts).
examples: Physical: color, density, melting point, conductivity
Chemical: flammability, reactivity with acid, tendency to rust

lessons.title: Physical vs. Chemical Changes
lessons.content: Physical changes don't create new substances; chemical changes do.
examples: Physical: ice melting, tearing paper, dissolving salt
Chemical: burning wood, rusting iron, baking a cake
Evidence of chemical change: color change, gas production, heat/light, precipitate

title: Mixtures and Solutions
description: Understand mixtures, solutions, and methods of separation.

lessons.title: Mixtures vs. Solutions
lessons.content: A mixture combines substances physically; a solution is a uniform mixture.
examples: Heterogeneous mixture: trail mix, salad, soil
Homogeneous mixture (solution): salt water, lemonade, air

lessons.title: Separation Methods
lessons.content: Mixtures can be separated using physical methods.
examples: Filtration: separates solids from liquids
Evaporation: removes water to leave dissolved solids
Magnetism: separate iron filings from sand
Distillation: separate liquids with different boiling points

title: Force and Motion
description: Investigate forces and their effects on motion.
objectives: Define force and describe its types
Explain Newton's First and Second Laws

lessons.title: Types of Forces
lessons.content: Forces are pushes or pulls that can change an object's motion.
examples: Contact forces: friction, tension, normal force
Non-contact forces: gravity, magnetism, electrostatic force

lessons.title: Newton's Laws
lessons.content: Newton's laws describe how forces affect motion.
examples: First Law: Objects in motion stay in motion unless acted on by a net force (inertia)
Second Law: F = ma (force = mass × acceleration)
Third Law: For every action there is an equal and opposite reaction

title: Ecosystems and Food Webs
description: Explore ecosystems, energy flow, and the impact of humans on ecosystems.
objectives: Explain energy flow through trophic levels

lessons.title: Food Chains and Webs
lessons.content: Energy flows from producers to consumers in a food chain; food webs show complex relationships.
examples: Grass → rabbit → fox → decomposer
Producers make their own food (photosynthesis); consumers eat others
Apex predators are at the top of the food chain

lessons.title: Ecosystem Disruption
lessons.content: Removing or adding species can cascade through the whole ecosystem.
examples: Wolf reintroduction in Yellowstone: changed deer behavior → restored plants → changed rivers
Invasive species: cane toads in Australia wiped out native predators

title: Earth's Systems — Water Cycle
description: Trace water through the hydrological cycle and explain its importance.
objectives: Describe each stage of the water cycle
Explain how the water cycle distributes fresh water
Connect the water cycle to weather patterns

lessons.title: The Water Cycle
lessons.content: Water continuously moves between Earth's surface and atmosphere.
examples: Evaporation: liquid water becomes water vapor
Condensation: water vapor becomes liquid (clouds)
Precipitation: water falls as rain, snow, sleet, or hail
Transpiration: plants release water vapor through leaves

lessons.title: Freshwater Distribution
lessons.content: Most of Earth's water is unusable; the water cycle is vital for freshwater supply.
examples: Only ~3% of Earth's water is fresh; most is frozen
Groundwater replenishment depends on precipitation infiltrating the soil

title: Earth's Layers and Plate Tectonics
description: Describe Earth's interior structure and the theory of plate tectonics.
objectives: Explain plate movement and its consequences

lessons.title: Earth's Layers
lessons.content: Earth has four main layers with different compositions and properties.
examples: Crust: thin outer layer of rock (5–70 km)
Mantle: thick layer of semi-solid rock (~2,900 km)
Outer core: liquid iron and nickel
Inner core: solid iron and nickel (temperatures ~5,400°C)

lessons.title: Plate Tectonics
lessons.content: Earth's crust is divided into moving plates that interact at boundaries.
examples: Convergent: plates collide → mountains or subduction zones
Divergent: plates separate → rift valleys or mid-ocean ridges
Transform: plates slide past → earthquakes (San Andreas Fault)

title: Energy Transformations
description: Identify types of energy and how energy transforms from one form to another.

lessons.title: Types of Energy
lessons.content: Energy exists in many forms and can transfer between them.
examples: Kinetic: energy of motion
Potential: stored energy (gravitational, elastic, chemical)
Thermal, electromagnetic, nuclear, sound energy

lessons.title: Energy Transformations
lessons.content: Energy changes form but is never created or destroyed.
examples: Light bulb: electrical → light + thermal
Car: chemical (fuel) → mechanical (motion) + thermal
Solar panel: light → electrical

title: Human Body Systems
description: Explore the major human body systems and how they interact.
objectives: Name and describe major body systems
Connect lifestyle choices to body system health

lessons.title: Body Systems
lessons.content: The body has 11 organ systems that work together.
examples: Circulatory: heart, blood vessels, blood — transports nutrients and oxygen
Respiratory: lungs — oxygen/CO2 exchange
Digestive: breaks down food into nutrients
Nervous: brain, spinal cord, nerves — control and communication

lessons.title: System Interactions
lessons.content: No system works alone; they are all interdependent.
examples: Running: respiratory (more O2), circulatory (faster heart), muscular, nervous, skeletal — all involved simultaneously

title: Genetics — Traits and Heredity
description: Understand how traits are inherited from parents to offspring.
objectives: Define gene, chromosome, DNA, and trait
Predict offspring traits using a Punnett square

lessons.title: DNA and Genes
lessons.content: DNA is the molecule that carries genetic information in every living cell.
examples: DNA is organized into chromosomes; humans have 46 (23 pairs)
A gene is a section of DNA that codes for a trait
You inherit one copy of each gene from each parent

lessons.title: Dominant and Recessive Traits
lessons.content: Some alleles are dominant (always expressed if present); others are recessive (only expressed when two copies are present).
examples: Brown eyes (B) dominant over blue eyes (b)
BB or Bb → brown eyes; bb → blue eyes
Punnett square: cross Bb × Bb → 25% BB, 50% Bb, 25% bb

title: Environmental Science — Sustainability
description: Explore sustainability, environmental challenges, and solutions.

lessons.title: Environmental Challenges
lessons.content: Human activity has created major environmental problems.
examples: Deforestation: loss of biodiversity, carbon release, disrupted water cycle
Ocean plastic: over 8 million tonnes enter oceans each year
Climate change: warming temperatures, extreme weather, sea level rise

lessons.title: Sustainable Solutions
lessons.content: Sustainability means meeting today's needs without compromising the future.
examples: Renewable energy: solar, wind, hydroelectric replaces fossil fuels
Circular economy: design products to be reused/recycled
Rewilding: restoring natural ecosystems
